extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents/applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Form paragraphs and examiner guidance for making and explaining rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness), including special situations (common ownership, joint research agreements, provisional rejections, combining references) and the factual test for obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.06 Notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the determination of the status of the application as subject to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (or as subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103) is incorrect, any correction of the statutory basis (i.e., changing from AIA to pre-AIA) for the rejection will not be considered a new ground of rejection if the prior art relied upon, and the rationale supporting the rejection, would be the same under either status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) This form paragraph must be used in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claims priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013. (2) This form paragraph should only be used ONCE in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.fti Statement of Statutory Basis, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a): '(a) A patent may not be obtained though the invention is not identically disclosed or described as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the subject matter sought to be patented and the prior art are such that the subject matter as a whole would have been obvious at the time the invention was made to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which said subject matter pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) The statute is not to be cited in all Office actions. It is only required in first actions on the merits employing pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) and final rejections. Where the statute is being applied, but is not cited in an action on the merits, use paragraph 7.103. (2) This form paragraph should only be used ONCE in a given Office action. (3) This form paragraph must precede form paragraphs 7.20.01.fti - 7.22.fti when used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.01.fti Pre-AIA 103(a) Rejection Using Prior Art Under Pre-AIA 102(e),(f), or (g) That Is Not Disqualified Under Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) Because Reference Is Prior Art Under Another Subsection of Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Template stating applicant provided a submission of common ownership or joint research agreement but the reference qualifies as prior art under another subsection of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102, and therefore is not disqualified under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Applicant may overcome the applied art either by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed therein was derived from the inventor of this application, or by antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Must be included following form paragraph 7.20.fti in all actions containing rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) using art disqualified under 103(c) using pre-AIA 102(e),(f), or (g), but which qualifies under another section of pre-AIA 102. (2) In bracket 1, identify the common assignee. (3) In bracket 2, identify the reference which has been disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.02.fti Joint Inventors, Common Ownership Presumed
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application names joint inventors, the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time any inventions covered therein were made absent evidence to the contrary. Applicant is advised of the obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates of each claim not commonly owned so the examiner can consider applicability of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and potential pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) or (g) prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This paragraph must be used in all applications with joint inventors (unless the claims are clearly restricted to only one claimed invention, e.g., only a single claim is presented in the application).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.04.fti Pre-AIA 103(a) Rejection Using Prior Art Under Pre-AIA 102(e),(f), or (g) That Is Attempted To Be Disqualified Under Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) Using the Common Ownership or Assignment Provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Template advising applicant has attempted to disqualify a reference under pre-AIA 103(c) by showing common ownership/assignment but failed to provide a statement that the application and the reference were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person at the time the invention was made in a conspicuous manner; therefore the reference is not disqualified. Applicant must file the required submission to properly disqualify the reference. Also notes applicant may overcome the applied art via 37 CFR 1.132 or antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Must be included in all actions containing rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where an attempt has been made to disqualify the reference under 103(c) but applicant has not provided a proper statement indicating common ownership or assignment at the time the invention was made. (2) In brackets 1 and 2, identify the commonly owned applied art (e.g., patent or co-pending application) and the applied art to be identified respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.05.fti Pre-AIA 103(a) Rejection Using Prior Art Under Pre-AIA 102(e),(f), or (g) That Is Attempted To Be Disqualified Under Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) Using the Joint Research Agreement Provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Template advising applicant attempted to disqualify a reference under pre-AIA 103(c) by showing the invention was subject to a joint research agreement at the time made but failed to provide required information. Applicant must file missing requirements to properly disqualify the reference. Applicant may alternatively overcome the applied art via 37 CFR 1.132 or antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Must be included in all actions containing rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where an attempt has been made to disqualify under 103(c) using joint research agreement provisions but the disqualification attempt is ineffective. (2) In bracket 1, identify the reference sought to be disqualified. (3) In bracket 2, identify the reason(s) the disqualification attempt is ineffective (e.g., noncompliance with statutory or rule requirements, failure to submit required statements, failure to amend specification to include party names). See 37 CFR 1.71(g), 1.104(c), and MPEP § 2146.02 and related subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.fti Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template rejection language: 'Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [2].' An explanation of the rejection must follow this form paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) This paragraph must be preceded by either form paragraph 7.20.fti or form paragraph 7.103. (2) An explanation of the rejection must follow; see MPEP § 2144. (3) If rejection relies upon prior art under pre-AIA 102(e), use pre-AIPA 102(e) as amended by AIPA to determine reference's prior art date unless reference is a US patent issued from international application with filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000; see related form paragraphs (7.12.fti, 7.12.01.fti). (4) If applicability of rejection prevents disqualification under 103(c), form paragraph 7.20.01.fti must follow. (5) If this is a provisional rejection based on a copending application that would comprise prior art under 102(e) if patented/published, use 7.21.01.fti instead. (6) In bracket 1 insert claim numbers; (7) in bracket 2 insert prior art relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.01.fti Provisional Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), Common Assignee, Common Applicant, or at Least One Common (Joint) Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Template stating claim(s) are provisionally rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over copending application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application; the copending application would constitute prior art under pre-AIA 102(e) if published or patented. The provisional rejection is based on presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application. Applicant may overcome by showing derivation under 37 CFR 1.132, antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a), or showing disqualification under 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Used to provisionally reject claims not patentably distinct from disclosure in a copending application that would be prior art under pre-AIA 102(e) if published/issued and also has a common assignee, common applicant (35 U.S.C. 118), or at least one common inventor. Should not be used when copending application is disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c). See MPEP § 2146.03(a). (2) Use pre-AIA 102(e) as amended by AIPA to determine copending application's prior art date unless copending application is based on an international application with filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000. (3) If claimed invention is fully disclosed in copending application, use paragraph 7.15.01.fti. (4) In bracket 1 insert claim numbers; bracket 2 application number; bracket 3 --assignee--, --applicant--, or --joint inventor--. (5) In bracket 4 insert an explanation of obviousness; see MPEP § 2144. (6) If not patentably distinct from invention claimed in copending application, add provisional obviousness double patenting rejection using form paragraphs 8.33 and 8.37. (7) Additionally make a rejection under 103(a) using 7.21.fti if evidence indicates copending application is also prior art under 102(f) or (g) and copending application not disqualified under 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.02.fti Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), Common Assignee, Common Applicant, or at Least One Common (Joint) Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Template: 'Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the pre-AIA 102(e) date of the reference, it constitutes prior art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of this application; (2) showing a date of invention for the claimed subject matter corresponding to subject matter disclosed but not claimed in the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) stating that the application and reference are currently owned by the same party and that the inventive entity named is the prior inventor under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 104 (as in effect Mar 15, 2013), together with a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c). This rejection might also be overcome by showing the reference is disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c). See MPEP § 2146 et seq. Examiner Notes: (1) Use when rejecting over a reference that discloses the claimed invention and only qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 102(e). Do not use if the reference qualifies under 102(a) or (b) (use 7.21.fti instead). Reference must have common assignee, common applicant, or at least one common inventor. (2) Guidance on applying pre-AIA vs pre-AIPA 102(e) dates and related bracket insertions: bracket 1 = claim numbers; bracket 2 = prior art references; bracket 3 = --assignee--, --applicant--, or --joint inventor--; bracket 4 = explanation of obviousness (see MPEP § 2144).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.22.fti Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), Further in View Of
rubrics_metrics.description: Template: 'Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [2] as applied to claim [3] above, and further in view of [4].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.21.fti. (2) An explanation of the rejection must follow; see MPEP § 2144. (3) If the rejection relies upon prior art under pre-AIA 102(e), apply pre-AIPA 102(e) rules to determine reference's date as described elsewhere (see form paragraphs 7.12.fti and 7.12.01.fti). Insert appropriate claim/reference identifiers in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.23.fti Test for Obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarizes the factual inquiries for establishing a background for determining obviousness under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a): (1) Determining the scope and contents of the prior art. (2) Ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue. (3) Resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art. (4) Considering objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This form paragraph may be used, if appropriate, in response to an argument regarding the applicability of the factors for determining obviousness. These four Graham factors form the core factual inquiries supporting a prima facie case of obviousness and must be addressed in the explanation of rejections (see MPEP § 2144 for supporting rationale).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.27.fti Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 or Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template allowing a combined rejection: 'Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 ([2]) as anticipated by or, in the alternative, under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over [3].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Not intended to be commonly used as substitute for a rejection under 102; prefer single rejection under either 102 or 103(a) when possible using appropriate form paragraphs. (2) Examples where paragraph may be used: dispute in claim interpretation (different interpretations lead to 102 vs 103), reference discloses all limitations except a property/function where inherent possession unclear (In re Fitzgerald), genus-species situations where species may be obvious even if genus not anticipatory (In re Schaumann), product-by-process issues (In re Marosi, In re Thorpe), means-plus-function uncertainty, overlapping ranges. (3) If claim interpretation renders claim indefinite, consider rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b). (4) Bracket instructions: bracket 1 = claim numbers; bracket 2 = appropriate paragraph letters; bracket 3 = prior art reference relied upon. (5) A full explanation should follow. (6) If relying on pre-AIA 102(e), apply pre-AIPA rules as described elsewhere. (7) Must be preceded by 7.07.fti and appropriate supporting form paragraphs (7.08.fti-7.14.fti) and form paragraph 7.20.fti or 7.103. (8) For transition applications with filing/priority complexities, include form paragraph 7.06 when required.
